title: quest browser outlives its workspace indefinitely: three daemons alive, one for 44 hours, all with deleted working directories
description:
Reported by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-18 and CONFIRMED HERE by direct process inspection rather than from their report. A quest browser daemon keeps running after the workspace it was started against has been deleted, with no upper bound observed.

Measured on this host at 2026-09-19T00:30Z, all three orphaned to init (ppid 1):

  pid    started                    elapsed       binary
  51327  Fri Sep 18 19:07:21 2026   22m           global install
  92526  Thu Sep 17 15:02:16 2026   1d 04:27      global install
  95162  Wed Sep 16 22:38:57 2026   1d 20:50      candidate install under .opum-candidates/0.7.1-pair

Every cwd is a deleted temp workspace of the form /private/var/folders/.../opum-e2e-ws-*/quest-project-*. lsof on a live .quest shows they hold no workspace open; they are simply alive.

TWO FACTS THAT NARROW IT, both measured rather than inferred:

1. The instances span TWO DIFFERENT INSTALLS -- one global, one a candidate install under .opum-candidates -- so nothing about how a candidate is bound explains it.

2. All three were spawned by opum-cli-e2e harness runs, including pid 51327 from their control matrix tonight. That explains the INSTANCES, not the BEHAVIOUR. A browser that outlives its workspace by 44 hours is a quest defect regardless of who started it; the harness spawning them is why there are three rather than why they survive. opum-cli-e2e made this split themselves and filed the reaping half as their TASK-91, which stays theirs.

An earlier suspicion that this repository own test suite leaks one was checked and is WRONG: every cwd is an opum-e2e-ws path, and this repository tests run bun src/cli/main.ts rather than an installed binary. Recorded because it was the obvious first guess.

NOT investigated yet: whether browser --port 0 --json installs any parent-death or workspace-death watch at all, whether the daemon should exit when its root disappears, and whether it should exit when its parent does. The daemons were deliberately left running for inspection -- opum-cli-e2e offered to kill them and was asked to hold.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The conditions under which quest browser should terminate are decided and written down -- at minimum whether it exits when the workspace root it was started against no longer exists.

A browser started against a workspace that is then deleted terminates rather than running indefinitely, proven by a test that creates a workspace, starts the daemon, removes the workspace and observes the exit.

Every leaked daemon alive on this host at fix time is reaped -- enumerated at that moment rather than against the count in this record, which was three when filed and four an hour later. The decision about parent-death behaviour is recorded even if the answer is that no parent watch is wanted.

plan: 1. Ruling (orchestrator 88b5699c, 2026-09-28, being recorded in opum-doc): exit when the workspace root it was started against no longer exists; no parent-death watch; reap the leaked daemons enumerated at fix time.

2. startBrowserServer takes an injected workspace-presence probe and a poll interval; the application layer stays fs-free. An unref-ed timer polls it; when the root is gone the server closes every connection and itself, so nothing holds the event loop and the process exits. The CLI passes a stat of the resolved worktree root that reports gone only on ENOENT/ENOTDIR.
3. Test: real process, temp workspace, start browser --port 0 --json, rm -rf the workspace, observe the process exit; plus the unit-level stays-up-while-present case.
4. Write the termination conditions into the browser help and the CHANGELOG. Enumerate and reap leaked quest browser daemons on this host at fix time, recording what was found.
implementationNotes:
EVIDENCE CORRECTED AND STRENGTHENED by opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-19. The description above says three daemons; there are FOUR, and the leak rate is now measured rather than inferred.

WHAT CHANGED. I filed this with three daemons and declined to carry a per-run frequency claim, because my process list could not support one -- the cwds are deleted, so nothing on my side tied a daemon to a particular run. I suggested matching the workspace token against their run log as the way to turn the inference into evidence. Their harness does record the workspace, so the match was available:

  pid 44029  19:35:00   opum-e2e-ws-TtCncZ -> runs/prepublish-quest0.9.0-lore0.8.0
  pid 51327  19:07:21   opum-e2e-ws-fiYBLC -> runs/control-darwin-arm64-quest0.7.1-lore0.7.0
  pid 92526  Thu 15:02  opum-e2e-ws-fvZFgk -> NONE FOUND (run directory not retained)
  pid 95162  Wed 22:38  opum-e2e-ws-AsWOco -> runs/2026-09-17T03-38-20-663Z

FOUR daemons, FOUR distinct workspaces, no workspace appearing twice. That is one per matrix run established BY NAME rather than by arithmetic, which is a different and better claim than the one either of us started with.

TWO CORRECTIONS RECORDED AS CORRECTIONS RATHER THAN SILENTLY APPLIED:

1. Their attribution of pid 51327 was backwards. They believed it came from the pre-publish qualification run; it is from the CONTROL run. The pre-publish daemon is pid 44029, which did not exist when I measured.

2. My count of three was accurate WHEN TAKEN and is stale rather than wrong. The fourth daemon started at 19:35, after my observation; they ran exactly one matrix in the interval, so the count moving from three to four is itself corroboration of the one-per-run rate rather than a discrepancy needing explanation. A dated measurement going stale is the normal way a dated measurement ends.

A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING WORTH ITS OWN FIX. One daemon (fvZFgk) matched nothing, because runs/ is gitignored and older run directories get cleaned. So ATTRIBUTION HAS A SHELF LIFE: a leaked process whose only identifier is a deleted cwd AND a discarded run directory cannot be attributed at all. The fix for the leak and the fix for the attribution window are different fixes, and the second one is invisible until someone tries to attribute an old process and cannot.

SCOPE UNCHANGED. The daemon behaviour is still this repository defect and the reaping half is still theirs (their TASK-91). Four daemons are deliberately left running for inspection; they will not reap without asking.

PREMISE CORRECTED AT FIX TIME, 2026-09-28. Measured before reaping anything; the reap is on hold. The description says "Every cwd is a deleted temp workspace". That is false for every daemon alive now, and the same-inode result means it was very likely false when filed too.

Enumerated on this host: 16 orphaned quest browser --port 0 --json daemons (ppid 1), started between Sep 16 22:38 and Sep 25 04:12. Four of them (95162, 92526, 51327, 44029) are the ones this record named. For each daemon, lsof gives the cwd inode, and stat gives the current inode of the same path. The result was 16 read, 16 SAME-INODE, 0 different, 0 gone, 0 unreadable, and every directory still holds .quest/. So these workspaces were never deleted or replaced. They are live, initialized workspaces that the harness left behind: $TMPDIR holds 1619 opum-e2e-ws-* directories. Script: scratchpad inode.sh, bash. A first zsh attempt reported all 16 GONE. That was a broken measurement, not a finding: it assigned `path`, which zsh ties to PATH, so every stat failed. It is recorded so nobody repeats it. The re-run printed its read count and an unreadable count, and it read all 16.

CONSEQUENCE. The ruled fix (exit when the workspace root no longer exists) is correct and is proven by test. But it would NOT have stopped ANY of the 16 daemons alive today, because none of their workspaces is gone. The actual leak is that the harness neither stops the daemon nor deletes the workspace. AC1 and AC2 are delivered as ruled. AC3 (reap) and whether quest needs a further bound (idle timeout, or the parent watch that was ruled out) are routed back to the orchestrator, because the ruling rested on the deleted-workspace premise. opum-cli-e2e is told as well, since the processes and workspaces are theirs (TASK-91).

EVIDENCE for AC1/AC2. test/qcli348-browser-exits-with-workspace.test.ts starts a real `bun src/cli/main.ts browser --port 0 --json` in a temp workspace. It confirms the browser serves /overview with 200 and is still running 3s later, then rm -rf the workspace and requires exit 0 within 10s. Against the pre-change source, the process was "still running" 10s after the deletion, so the test failed. After the change it exits 0. A unit test pins that a probe error keeps the server up and only a false closes it. The conditions are written into `quest help browser` and the CHANGELOG. bun run check: 860 pass, 0 fail.

AC3 REAPED, 2026-09-28, under opum-agent's ruling (orchestrator 88b5699c): reap the processes, leave the directories. The 1,619 opum-e2e-ws-* directories belong to opum-cli-e2e and were NOT touched. opum-cli-e2e was told before the kill. opum-agent independently confirmed that every daemon started before opum-cli-e2e's TASK-91 fix (#278, 2026-09-25T11:30Z), so this is pre-fix residue, not a regression. The same ruling says quest needs no further bound (no idle timeout); revisit only if a daemon appears with a start time after that fix.

The filter was re-enumerated at kill time: the command ends in exactly `/bin/quest browser --port 0 --json`, ppid is 1, and the cwd matches */opum-e2e-ws-*/*. BEFORE: 16 matched, the same 16 pids as the earlier inode measurement. AFTER (3s after SIGTERM): 0 matched. A separate count of every process containing "quest browser" read 17 before and 1 after, then 0 on an immediate re-read. That 17th did not match the filter: no SKIP line was printed, so it was not a browser with some other cwd. It exited on its own. It is recorded as unidentified rather than explained. The pid list is in the session scratchpad reap-before.txt. Only SIGTERM was sent. Every daemon exited on it, and none needed SIGKILL.
finalSummary: quest browser now exits when the workspace root it was started against no longer exists. An unref-ed 2s poll stats the root, and on ENOENT/ENOTDIR closes the server and every connection, so the process exits. There is no parent-death watch. Both conditions are in quest help browser. This was ruled in opum-doc docs/adr/exit-the-quest-browser-daemon-when-its-workspace-root-disappears.md (0d847e5). It is proven by a real-process test that deletes the workspace and requires exit 0; that test failed on the pre-change source. Premise correction at fix time: the 16 leaked daemons alive today all had EXISTING workspaces (same inode, .quest present). So the fix would not have stopped them, and the original "deleted cwd" claim was very likely never true. On a second ruling (no further bound, since they predate the opum-cli-e2e TASK-91 fix), all 16 processes were reaped: 16 before, 0 after, SIGTERM only, directories untouched. Delivered in opum-ai/quest-cli#361.
